vocabulary: Water table: the top of the saturated zone in an unconfined aquifer.

description: Signature edition. overview: In the Signature teaching of hydrogeology, Potentiometric mapping is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Hydraulic head means the water level defining which way groundwater flows, always downhill in head. Well hydraulics means drawdown cones and the Theis solution describing pumping effects. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Advanced material that follows.
core_concepts: Hydraulic head: the water level defining which way groundwater flows, always downhill in head.
Well hydraulics: drawdown cones and the Theis solution describing pumping effects.
key_laws: Ghyben-Herzberg relation: freshwater lens thickness about forty times its height above sea level.
Darcy's law: specific discharge equals hydraulic conductivity times hydraulic gradient.
vocabulary: Safe yield: pumping that can continue indefinitely without unacceptable consequences.
Piezometer: a well measuring hydraulic head at a point.
methods: Potentiometric mapping: contouring head measurements to draw flow directions.
history: Hydrogeology began with Darcy's 1856 sand-column experiments; Theis's 1935 transient well theory made pumping analysis quantitative. The 20th century added contaminant hydrogeology, and sustainable-yield management is now critical worldwide.
